dossier.public_summary: A 0.92-day dip repeating 53 times on a nearby M dwarf implies a 2.2 Earth-radius planet. The transit is flat-bottomed, centred, and evenly repeated with no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse, and centroiding shows the signal is on the star, not a nearby eclipsing binary.

reasons.why: difference imaging puts the dip on the target and rules out neighbours; suspects at 27.7, 27.5 arcsec are 13.9, 16.4 sigma from the centroid
sub-Neptune size with flat bottom, short U-shape and low impact parameter positively favours a planet over a V-shaped grazing binary; not near the star-size limit
no odd/even difference and no significant secondary at half period argue against an eclipsing binary at this period

53 consistent transits across 2 sectors with steady depth and low duration ratio and no top-3 domination support a planet rather than spots or a blend; signal repeats each observing season as required
